2.9 Camera Preview and Photo Capture

Live camera preview on the TFT screen with gesture controls and BMP photo capture to SD card.

Overview

This project integrates the OV2640 camera with LVGL to create a real-time viewfinder. You can see what the camera sees directly on the screen, capture photos to the SD card, and control camera settings with touch gestures.

What You’ll Learn

  • Streaming camera frames to an LVGL image object

  • Using FreeRTOS tasks for parallel camera frame grabbing

  • Double-buffering for tear-free display

  • Saving BMP images to SD card

  • Implementing swipe gestures (mirror/flip toggle)

How the Code Works

Camera Frame Grabber (FreeRTOS Task)

A separate FreeRTOS task continuously reads RGB565 frames from the camera and writes them into a double-buffer:

static void cameraTask(void *pvParameters) {
    while (true) {
        camera_fb_t *fb = esp_camera_fb_get();
        memcpy(buf[activeBuf], fb->buf, BUF_SIZE);
        esp_camera_fb_return(fb);
        frameReady = true;
        vTaskDelay(1);
    }
}

LVGL Image Display

The main LVGL task checks for a new frame and updates the image object (240×240 region):

if (frameReady) {
    lv_img_set_src(camera_img, buf[activeBuf]);
    frameReady = false;
    activeBuf = !activeBuf;  // Swap buffers
}

Photo Capture

Tapping the camera icon captures the current frame as a BMP file on the SD card.

Gesture Controls

  • Swipe left/right: toggle horizontal mirror

  • Swipe up/down: toggle vertical flip

Pin Connections

Same camera pinout as 1.7 Camera Web Server. SD card for saving photos.

Expected Result

  • Live 240×240 camera preview on the left side of the screen

  • Photo capture button on the right — tap to save a BMP to the SD card

  • Swipe gestures mirror/flip the preview

  • Tap the exit button to return

Note

The camera preview requires significant CPU and memory resources. The double-buffering approach ensures smooth, tear-free video.
